patient.purpose: Aim to control advanced lung cancer, relieve symptoms and prolong life where possible.
patient.context_label: Previously treated locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
patient.indication_text: Adults with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC after prior chemotherapy; recurrence or progression during or after one prior platinum-containing doublet for advanced/metastatic disease; ECOG 0–1.
patient.schedule_summary: Nivolumab 240 mg IV over 30 minutes OR 600 mg as a subcutaneous injection over 3–5 minutes on Day 1 every 2 weeks. Your team confirms one formulation; the whole visit includes checks and preparation. Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity, with individual benefit and safety review.
patient.administration_text: Nivolumab 240 mg IV over 30 minutes OR 600 mg as a subcutaneous injection over 3–5 minutes on Day 1 every 2 weeks. Your team confirms one formulation; the whole visit includes checks and preparation.
patient.monitoring_summary: Blood count, kidney/liver tests and glucose before every 2-week cycle; thyroid once a month; cortisol if clinically indicated. Review cancer progression before cycle 8. Continue immune-toxicity monitoring for at least 5 months after the last dose.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab blocks PD-1 on immune cells, helping them recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause inflammation in healthy organs.
agents.watch: Report new breathing, bowel, skin, hormone, heart or nerve symptoms promptly; these may be immune inflammation.
risks: Immune inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, hormone glands, skin, heart and nervous system
Some effects need steroids, hospital care or long-term hormone replacement

patient.urgent_extra: Contact the oncology team immediately for new or worsening breathlessness, chest pain, persistent diarrhoea, severe tummy pain, yellow skin/eyes, much less urine, severe headache, marked weakness, confusion, unusual thirst or passing much more urine, or a spreading/blistering rash. For severe breathing difficulty, collapse, seizure or other immediately dangerous symptoms, seek emergency care. Do not wait for the next infusion.
patient.consent_support: Discuss the aim for your exact lung setting, likely benefit, alternatives, important immune risks and how treatment may be paused or stopped. Some side effects need long-term medicines. Ask about fertility, pregnancy, breastfeeding and effects on daily life.
patient.safety_note: Immune effects can happen on any day and after treatment ends. Carry your immunotherapy alert card and tell any healthcare team that you receive nivolumab.

day_groups.title: Your treatment visit
day_groups.body: The team checks blood results, symptoms and medicines before the prescribed infusion or injection. Tell the nurse immediately about itching, flushing, breathlessness, dizziness or feeling suddenly unwell.
day_groups.action: Before leaving, confirm the next tests, treatment visit and urgent contact number.

day_groups.title: Between visits
day_groups.body: You may feel well between infusions, but immune inflammation can begin at any time. Keep a short symptom record and take medicines exactly as prescribed. Contact your team about new symptoms instead of waiting for your next appointment.
day_groups.action: Confirm monthly thyroid tests and who arranges them; report new symptoms without waiting for the next treatment.

support.title: Sickness medicines
support.text: Nivolumab alone has minimal sickness risk. Routine preventive anti-sickness medicines or premedication are not usually required; the team may prescribe symptom relief.

support.title: Immune alert card
support.text: Carry your alert card during treatment and afterwards. Show it when seeking urgent care; symptoms can be mistaken for an infection or an ordinary stomach upset.

support.title: Hormones and steroids
support.text: Some immune effects need steroids or hormone replacement. Follow the prescribed plan and do not stop steroids suddenly. Ask for help if symptoms worsen or you cannot take essential medicines.

support.title: Pregnancy and breastfeeding
support.text: Discuss pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding before treatment. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 5 months after the last dose. Breastfeeding requires a specialist decision; contact your team promptly if pregnancy occurs.

questions.q: Why am I having nivolumab?
questions.a: Previously treated locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). It is used after previous chemotherapy to help control cancer; ask how the benefits and alternatives apply to you.

questions.q: Which formulation and schedule will I receive?
questions.a: Nivolumab 240 mg IV over 30 minutes OR 600 mg as a subcutaneous injection over 3–5 minutes on Day 1 every 2 weeks. Your team confirms one formulation; the whole visit includes checks and preparation.

questions.q: How long will treatment continue?
questions.a: Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity, with individual benefit and safety review.

questions.q: Who arranges my tests and scans?
questions.a: Blood count, kidney/liver tests and glucose before every 2-week cycle; thyroid once a month; cortisol if clinically indicated. Review cancer progression before cycle 8. Continue immune-toxicity monitoring for at least 5 months after the last dose.

questions.q: When should I call the team?
questions.a: Report new breathlessness, persistent diarrhoea, severe pain, yellow eyes, reduced urine, severe headache, weakness, unusual thirst or a spreading/blistering rash immediately. Use your oncology contact plan; severe breathing difficulty, collapse, seizure or severe chest pain needs emergency care.

questions.q: What are my other options?
questions.a: Ask about other anticancer treatment, trials and symptom-focused care suited to your cancer and preferences. Support remains available if you decline treatment.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be offered
evidence.intro: Nivolumab can help the immune system control some previously treated lung cancers. Some people benefit for a long time; others do not benefit.
evidence.interpretation: Trial results describe groups, not an individual prognosis.
evidence.population: Previously treated locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
evidence.limitations: CheckMate 017/057 studied nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks versus docetaxel, after platinum. Fixed-dose q14/q28 and SC schedules are supported through dosing/formulation bridging, not separate randomised superiority estimates. The pooled lung results do not establish benefit for other tumours or first-line, perioperative or small-cell lung settings.

factors: Adults with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC after prior chemotherapy; recurrence or progression during or after one prior platinum-containing doublet for advanced/metastatic disease; ECOG 0–1.

limitations: CheckMate 017/057 studied nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks versus docetaxel, after platinum. Shared non-lung indications remain in the protocol; this patient/evidence suite is lung-focused.

key_points: No nivolumab dose escalation/reduction; use Table 3 organ-specific hold/stop pathways.

items.title: Eligibility
items.text: Adults with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC after prior chemotherapy; recurrence or progression during or after one prior platinum-containing doublet for advanced/metastatic disease; ECOG 0–1.

items.title: Treatment aim
items.text: Aim to control advanced lung cancer, relieve symptoms and prolong life where possible.

items.title: Choices
items.text: Discuss other treatment, trials and symptom-focused care with your team.

chapters.title: How nivolumab works
chapters.intro: Immunotherapy supports immune attack.

items.title: PD-1 blockade
items.text: Nivolumab blocks PD-1 on immune cells, helping them recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause the immune system to inflame healthy organs.

items.title: Healthy organs
items.text: Inflammation can affect lungs, bowel, liver, kidneys, skin, glands, muscles, heart and nerves. Some effects are serious, delayed or permanent.

chapters.title: Your treatment course
chapters.intro: Confirm the formulation with your team.

items.title: Administration
items.text: Nivolumab 480 mg IV over 60 minutes OR 1200 mg as a subcutaneous injection over 3–5 minutes on Day 1 every 4 weeks. Your team confirms one formulation; the whole visit includes checks and preparation.

items.title: Course length
items.text: Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity, with individual benefit and safety review.

items.title: Pauses
items.text: Treatment may be held or stopped for side effects. Nivolumab is not routinely dose-reduced. Tell the team about missed appointments.

chapters.title: Tests and review
chapters.intro: New symptoms matter even when recent tests were normal.

items.title: Before starting
items.text: Blood count, kidney/liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests establish a baseline; discuss existing illness and all medicines.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: Blood count, kidney/liver tests and glucose before every 4-week cycle; thyroid once a month; cortisol if clinically indicated. Review cancer progression before cycle 4. Continue immune-toxicity monitoring for at least 5 months after the last dose.

items.title: Response review
items.text: Your team assesses progression before cycle 4; later scans follow the consultant plan.

chapters.title: Practical support
chapters.intro: Tell your team what matters to you.

items.title: Energy and activity
items.text: Balance activity and rest. New marked fatigue with dizziness, headache, thirst or weakness needs assessment.

items.title: Medicines and pregnancy
items.text: Bring all medicine/supplement details. Discuss fertility and breastfeeding. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 5 months after the final dose.

items.title: Sickness
items.text: Minimal sickness risk: routine preventive sickness medicines are not usually required. Your team may prescribe symptom relief.

chapters.title: When to get help
chapters.intro: Use your oncology urgent contact plan.

items.title: Report promptly
items.text: Report new breathlessness, persistent diarrhoea, severe pain, yellow eyes, reduced urine, severe headache, weakness, unusual thirst or a spreading/blistering rash immediately. Use your oncology contact plan; severe breathing difficulty, collapse, seizure or severe chest pain needs emergency care.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: Tell the nurse immediately about a reaction during the infusion or injection.

items.title: After treatment
items.text: Continue monitoring for at least 5 months after the final dose. Show your immune alert card to anyone treating you.

patient.title: Nivolumab, ipilimumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin
patient.purpose: This treatment aims to control metastatic squamous non-small-cell lung cancer, help symptoms and extend life. It is usually given without an expectation of cure.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment.

agents.name: Ipilimumab
agents.explanation: Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another control on T-cell activity. It works alongside nivolumab through a different immune checkpoint. It is given every 42 days, so it is absent from each Day 22 visit. Healthy organs can also become inflamed.
agents.watch: Report diarrhoea, tummy pain, rash, severe tiredness, headache or other new symptoms promptly. Keep your immune alert card.
risks: Immune bowel, liver, skin and hormone inflammation

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: Paclitaxel stabilises microtubules, structures cells use during division. It can slow cancer growth but also harm healthy nerves, blood-forming cells and hair follicles. There are two planned doses.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse immediately about infusion symptoms. Report numbness, tingling, fever, painful muscles, mouth sores or diarrhoea.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Its dose depends on target exposure (AUC) and measured or estimated kidney function; AUC is not a fixed number of milligrams. There are two planned doses in this regimen.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, nausea, hearing changes or numbness. Tell the nurse immediately about possible allergy during the infusion.

phases.label: Cycle 1: two chemotherapy administrations
phases.detail: One 42-day cycle, chemotherapy Days 1 and 22 only. Cycle 1 lasts 42 days: nivolumab, ipilimumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin on Day 1; nivolumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin on Day 22. These are the only two planned chemotherapy administrations. From Cycle 2, nivolumab is given on Days 1 and 22 and ipilimumab on Day 1.

support.title: Cycle 1 Days 1 and 22 · chemotherapy-containing visits
support.text: Cycle 1 lasts 42 days: nivolumab, ipilimumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin on Day 1; nivolumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin on Day 22. These are the only two planned chemotherapy administrations. From Cycle 2, nivolumab is given on Days 1 and 22 and ipilimumab on Day 1. Paclitaxel premedication includes corticosteroid and antihistamine treatment, with H2-blocker decisions made by the team. The source allows consultant-directed changes; ask for a written plan for each of the two chemotherapy visits. The team must reconcile paclitaxel allergy-prevention steroids with anti-sickness steroids and the aprepitant interaction into one prescription. Do not add courses or take leftover steroids yourself. Use dedicated carboplatin AUC≥4 NCIS row; no routine olanzapine in that row. Myalgia/arthralgia may need an individual analgesia plan. Both immune medicines can inflame healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Keep your immune alert card and report new symptoms promptly, including for at least five months after the last dose.

support.text: Both immune medicines can inflame healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Keep your immune alert card and report new symptoms promptly, including for at least five months after the last dose. Chemotherapy is complete; review and stop induction prophylaxis rather than automatically repeating it.

support.title: Cycle 2 onwards · Day 22 nivolumab alone
support.text: Both immune medicines can inflame healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Keep your immune alert card and report new symptoms promptly, including for at least five months after the last dose.

questions.q: Why are the visits different?
questions.a: Cycle 1 lasts 42 days: nivolumab, ipilimumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin on Day 1; nivolumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin on Day 22. These are the only two planned chemotherapy administrations. From Cycle 2, nivolumab is given on Days 1 and 22 and ipilimumab on Day 1.

questions.q: How long is treatment planned?
questions.a: Continue while appropriate until progression, unacceptable toxicity or up to 24 months without progression. Your team reviews the plan and may delay or stop treatment.

questions.q: What if I miss a support medicine?
questions.a: Ask your oncology team or pharmacist for advice; do not double doses or combine steroid courses yourself.

questions.q: How is benefit checked?
questions.a: Your consultant sets the scan plan and reviews symptoms, results and priorities. Side effects do not reliably show cancer response.

questions.q: Can I decide from this guide whether treatment is safe today?
questions.a: No. The team must assess symptoms, blood results, previous reactions and the prescribing protocol.

questions.q: What should I report after treatment stops?
questions.a: Both immune medicines can inflame healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Keep your immune alert card and report new symptoms promptly, including for at least five months after the last dose.

items.title: Bowel, lungs and skin
items.text: New diarrhoea, tummy pain, blood/mucus in stool, cough, breathlessness, blistering or peeling skin need prompt assessment.

items.text: Unusual weakness, headache, dizziness, marked thirst, frequent urination, chest pain, palpitations, drooping eyelids or difficulty swallowing/breathing need urgent advice. Several organs can be inflamed together.

items.title: Chemotherapy effects
items.text: Paclitaxel/carboplatin can cause low blood counts, infection, hair loss, neuropathy, muscle pain, nausea and infusion reactions. Report symptoms before another dose.

items.title: Living with treatment

evidence.population: 719 previously untreated adults with stage IV/recurrent NSCLC without sensitising EGFR/ALK alterations; mixed squamous and non-squamous histologies.
evidence.comparison: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab and two cycles of histology-based platinum-doublet chemotherapy (361) versus four chemotherapy cycles (358); optional pemetrexed maintenance in the control non-squamous population.
evidence.applicability: Current 00712 is the squamous NSCLC carboplatin/paclitaxel strategy. CheckMate 9LA pooled squamous and non-squamous histologies; overall outcomes are not a squamous-only estimate. Source ECOG allows 0–2, while trial population was ECOG 0–1; benefit in ECOG 2 is not established by the randomized trial.

endpoints.metric: Overall randomized population, final six-year analysis
endpoints.result_text: HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.63–0.87); six-year survival 16% versus 10%, minimum follow-up 68.6 months.
endpoints.interpretation: Population-level randomized comparison of the complete treatment strategies, not a personal survival prediction or a cisplatin-versus-carboplatin comparison.
endpoints.analysis_status: Final six-year follow-up; published 29 May 2025.

endpoints.interpretation: Exploratory histology subgroup of randomized strategy; not a personal forecast and not a comparison with another immune regimen.
endpoints.analysis_status: Final follow-up subgroup analysis; retain subgroup limitations.

evidence.qualitative_result: The combined strategy improved survival compared with chemotherapy in the trial population, with some durable responses. Benefits and harms vary between people.
limitations: Open-label trial of complete strategies; overall estimates pool histologies.
NCCP ECOG 0–2 is broader than trial ECOG 0–1.
Subgroup analyses are exploratory; no cross-trial ranking or individualized survival inference.
evidence.harms: Combining chemotherapy with dual checkpoint blockade introduces cytotoxic and immune-mediated harms; important inflammation can affect multiple organs and require hospital care or permanent treatment cessation. Final follow-up reported no new safety signals; this does not imply no risk.

patient.title: Nivolumab and ipilimumab for pleural mesothelioma
patient.purpose: This treatment aims to control pleural mesothelioma that cannot be removed with curative surgery, help symptoms and extend life. It is usually given without an expectation of cure. Mesothelioma starts in the lining around the lung and is different from non-small-cell lung cancer.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment.

agents.name: Ipilimumab
agents.explanation: Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another control on T-cell activity. It works alongside nivolumab through a different immune checkpoint. It is given every 42 days, so it is absent from each Day 22 visit. Healthy organs can also become inflamed.
agents.watch: Report diarrhoea, tummy pain, rash, severe tiredness, headache or other new symptoms promptly. Keep your immune alert card.
risks: Immune bowel, liver, skin and hormone inflammation

phases.label: Dual immunotherapy
phases.detail: Until progression, unacceptable toxicity or up to 24 months without progression. Each cycle lasts 42 days: nivolumab and ipilimumab on Day 1, then nivolumab alone on Day 22. Nivolumab is every three weeks and ipilimumab every six weeks. This regimen contains no chemotherapy.

questions.q: How long is treatment planned?
questions.a: Continue while appropriate until progression, unacceptable toxicity or up to 24 months without progression. Your team reviews the plan and may delay or stop treatment.

questions.q: What if I miss a support medicine?
questions.a: Ask your oncology team or pharmacist for advice; do not double doses or combine steroid courses yourself.

questions.q: How is benefit checked?
questions.a: Your consultant sets the scan plan and reviews symptoms, results and priorities. Side effects do not reliably show cancer response.

questions.q: Can I decide from this guide whether treatment is safe today?

chapters.title: Why this treatment is offered
chapters.intro: This treatment aims to control pleural mesothelioma that cannot be removed with curative surgery, help symptoms and extend life. It is usually given without an expectation of cure. Mesothelioma starts in the lining around the lung and is different from non-small-cell lung cancer.

items.title: What does the diagnosis mean?
items.text: Pleural mesothelioma begins in the lining around the lung. The team confirms the subtype and that curative surgery is not suitable.

items.title: What are the alternatives?
items.text: Ask about other systemic options, trials and symptom-focused care in the context of your cancer, health and priorities.

chapters.title: Before the first visit
chapters.intro: Carry treatment details and the immune alert card. Describe your usual bowel pattern, breathing, energy, skin and hormone symptoms, and tell the team about autoimmune illness, infections and all medicines.

items.title: Your usual health
items.text: Describe usual bowel movements, breathing, energy and skin; report autoimmune illness, infection, nerve symptoms and every medicine or supplement.

items.title: Practical preparation
items.text: Arrange blood tests, transport and support at home. Keep treatment names, urgent contacts and your immune alert card available.

chapters.title: Alternating treatment visits
chapters.intro: Each cycle lasts 42 days: nivolumab and ipilimumab on Day 1, then nivolumab alone on Day 22. Nivolumab is every three weeks and ipilimumab every six weeks. This regimen contains no chemotherapy.

items.title: Duration
items.text: Continue while appropriate until progression, unacceptable toxicity or up to 24 months without progression. Your team reviews the plan and may delay or stop treatment.

items.title: Time in the unit
items.text: Nivolumab over 30 minutes, then ipilimumab over 30 minutes on Day 1 only. Ipilimumab vital signs are checked every 30 minutes during infusion and for an hour afterwards. Blood tests, preparation and observation add to time in the unit.

chapters.title: Checks before and during treatment
chapters.intro: Blood count, kidney, liver, glucose and thyroid tests before each 42-day cycle; symptoms reviewed before each infusion and additional tests when indicated. Cortisol if clinically indicated.

items.title: Before starting
items.text: Baseline FBC, renal/liver profile, glucose and TFTs; hepatitis B surface antigen and core antibody and hepatitis C RNA. Confirm no prior chemotherapy for pleural mesothelioma.

items.title: New symptoms
items.text: Extra tests may be needed between visits. Routine blood results alone cannot exclude every immune effect.

items.title: Response
items.text: Scans follow the consultant plan; discuss benefit, uncertainty and what would lead to changing treatment.

chapters.title: Treatment effects
chapters.intro: Both immune medicines can inflame healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Keep your immune alert card and report new symptoms promptly, including for at least five months after the last dose.

items.title: Bowel, lungs and skin
items.text: New diarrhoea, tummy pain, blood/mucus in stool, cough, breathlessness, blistering or peeling skin need prompt assessment.

items.title: Hormones, heart, muscles and nerves
items.text: Unusual weakness, headache, dizziness, marked thirst, frequent urination, chest pain, palpitations, drooping eyelids or difficulty swallowing/breathing need urgent advice. Several organs can be inflamed together.

items.title: Liver and kidneys
items.text: Yellow eyes or skin, dark urine, reduced urine or swelling need prompt review; blood tests can find changes before symptoms.

chapters.title: Support medicines and self-care
chapters.intro: Steroids may be prescribed to treat immune inflammation. Follow the exact dose and taper; do not start, stop or change them without your team. Hormone replacement can sometimes be long term.

items.title: Your plan
items.text: Carry treatment details and the immune alert card. Describe your usual bowel pattern, breathing, energy, skin and hormone symptoms, and tell the team about autoimmune illness, infections and all medicines.

items.title: When unwell
items.text: Follow your oncology emergency instructions for fever, shivering or sudden illness even with a normal temperature. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or confusion needs emergency care.

chapters.title: After treatment and daily life
chapters.intro: Both immune medicines can inflame healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Keep your immune alert card and report new symptoms promptly, including for at least five months after the last dose.

items.title: Reproductive advice
items.text: Discuss pregnancy, breastfeeding, fertility and contraception before treatment. Effective contraception is needed for at least five months after the last nivolumab dose; ask about your individual plan.

items.title: Living with treatment
items.text: Ask for help with fatigue, appetite, pain, breathlessness, work and emotional concerns. Follow-up continues for unresolved effects and any long-term hormone replacement.

evidence.title: Why this treatment is offered
evidence.intro: In CheckMate 743, nivolumab plus ipilimumab improved overall survival compared with platinum/pemetrexed chemotherapy in previously untreated unresectable pleural mesothelioma.
evidence.interpretation: Trial results compare groups and cannot predict your personal benefit. Discuss how the study population relates to your cancer and health.
evidence.population: 605 adults with previously untreated unresectable pleural mesothelioma (epithelioid and non-epithelioid), ECOG 0–1; 303 assigned nivolumab/ipilimumab and 302 chemotherapy.
evidence.limitations: No personal survival estimate or cross-trial ranking.

evidence.population: 605 adults with previously untreated unresectable pleural mesothelioma (epithelioid and non-epithelioid), ECOG 0–1; 303 assigned nivolumab/ipilimumab and 302 chemotherapy.
evidence.comparison: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg every two weeks plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every six weeks for up to two years versus up to six cycles of platinum/pemetrexed chemotherapy.
evidence.applicability: Supports first-line dual immunotherapy for unresectable pleural mesothelioma. NCCP uses nivolumab 360 mg every three weeks, a licensed alternative schedule; the randomized trial itself used 3 mg/kg every two weeks. Not evidence for non-pleural mesothelioma or a later-line indication.

endpoints.result_text: Five-year survival 14% versus 6%; HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.62–0.88). Median OS 18.1 versus 14.1 months; median follow-up 66.8 months.
endpoints.interpretation: Randomized group comparison, not a personal prognosis. No head-to-head inference against other immunotherapy combinations.
endpoints.analysis_status: Published March 2026; June and September 2026 errata checked. Main OS estimate unchanged.

evidence.qualitative_result: In CheckMate 743, nivolumab plus ipilimumab improved overall survival compared with platinum/pemetrexed chemotherapy in previously untreated unresectable pleural mesothelioma.
limitations: Open-label comparison; 24% of the chemotherapy group subsequently received immunotherapy. Adjusted treatment-switching analyses are exploratory and are not substituted for the randomized HR.
Histology subgroups must not be presented as a randomized comparison between histologies.
June correction changes Figure 2D chemotherapy sample size to 76; September corrections address demographic/biomarker and supplementary subgroup figure reporting. Do not reuse uncorrected figures.
The trial and NCCP nivolumab schedules differ; product-information pharmacokinetic/safety support underlies the licensed 360 mg every-three-week schedule.
harms: Dual checkpoint blockade can cause severe or fatal immune inflammation, including delayed effects and lasting endocrine replacement needs. Trial averages do not replace individual risk assessment.

patient.title: Nivolumab and selected platinum chemotherapy before surgery
patient.purpose: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment.

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: Paclitaxel stabilises microtubules, structures cells use during division. It can slow cancer growth but also harm healthy nerves, blood-forming cells and hair follicles. There are up to three planned doses.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse immediately about infusion symptoms. Report numbness, tingling, fever, painful muscles, mouth sores or diarrhoea.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Its dose depends on target exposure (AUC) and measured or estimated kidney function; AUC is not a fixed number of milligrams. There are two planned doses in this regimen.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, nausea, hearing changes or numbness. Tell the nurse immediately about possible allergy during the infusion.

patient.title: Nivolumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin before surgery
patient.purpose: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment.

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: Paclitaxel stabilises microtubules, structures cells use during division. It can slow cancer growth but also harm healthy nerves, blood-forming cells and hair follicles. There are up to three planned doses.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse immediately about infusion symptoms. Report numbness, tingling, fever, painful muscles, mouth sores or diarrhoea.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Its dose depends on target exposure (AUC) and measured or estimated kidney function; AUC is not a fixed number of milligrams. There are two planned doses in this regimen.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, nausea, hearing changes or numbness. Tell the nurse immediately about possible allergy during the infusion.

questions.q: Will I receive all five combinations?
questions.a: No. This guide is for paclitaxel and carboplatin with nivolumab. The five backbones are alternatives; your team prescribes one.

questions.q: Does nivolumab continue after surgery?
questions.a: Not automatically under this NCCP regimen. It covers at most three cycles before surgery; any later treatment needs a separate plan.

questions.q: What if a dose is delayed?
questions.a: The team reviews blood tests, symptoms and recovery. Do not assume a delay means treatment has failed or that surgery must occur on a fixed date.

items.title: Why these medicines?
items.text: Nivolumab helps immune cells recognise cancer; chemotherapy damages dividing cells. Your prescribed backbone is paclitaxel and carboplatin.

items.text: In a randomized study, adding nivolumab to chemotherapy before surgery improved survival compared with chemotherapy alone. Your team considers the exact cancer, test results, fitness and preferences.

patient.title: Nivolumab, gemcitabine and carboplatin before surgery
patient.purpose: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment.

agents.name: Gemcitabine
agents.explanation: Gemcitabine interferes with making DNA, which dividing cancer cells need. Healthy blood-forming cells and other tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report fever, unusual bleeding, breathlessness, rash, swelling or reduced urine promptly.
risks: Rare serious lung or kidney injury

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Its dose depends on target exposure (AUC) and measured or estimated kidney function; AUC is not a fixed number of milligrams. There are two planned doses in this regimen.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, nausea, hearing changes or numbness. Tell the nurse immediately about possible allergy during the infusion.

questions.q: Will I receive all five combinations?
questions.a: No. This guide is for gemcitabine and carboplatin with nivolumab. The five backbones are alternatives; your team prescribes one.

questions.q: Does nivolumab continue after surgery?
questions.a: Not automatically under this NCCP regimen. It covers at most three cycles before surgery; any later treatment needs a separate plan.

questions.q: What if a dose is delayed?
questions.a: The team reviews blood tests, symptoms and recovery. Do not assume a delay means treatment has failed or that surgery must occur on a fixed date.

chapters.title: Your treatment before surgery
chapters.intro: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

items.title: Why these medicines?
items.text: Nivolumab helps immune cells recognise cancer; chemotherapy damages dividing cells. Your prescribed backbone is gemcitabine and carboplatin.

items.title: Evidence and uncertainty
items.text: In a randomized study, adding nivolumab to chemotherapy before surgery improved survival compared with chemotherapy alone. Your team considers the exact cancer, test results, fitness and preferences.

items.text: Discuss surgery and other suitable treatments, clinical trials and the option of not proceeding; choices depend on the multidisciplinary assessment.

patient.title: Nivolumab, gemcitabine and cisplatin before surgery
patient.purpose: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment.

agents.name: Gemcitabine
agents.explanation: Gemcitabine interferes with making DNA, which dividing cancer cells need. Healthy blood-forming cells and other tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report fever, unusual bleeding, breathlessness, rash, swelling or reduced urine promptly.
risks: Rare serious lung or kidney injury

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with copying and repair. This helps stop cancer cells dividing, but healthy tissues may also be affected. Kidney protection with fluids and monitoring is central to cisplatin treatment.
agents.watch: Report ringing in the ears, hearing changes, numbness or loss of function. Tell the team if you cannot drink, are passing less urine or become swollen or breathless during fluids.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Hearing changes or tinnitus, which can persist
Numbness or tingling, which can persist
Electrolyte changes and need for hydration

questions.q: Will I receive all five combinations?
questions.a: No. This guide is for gemcitabine and cisplatin with nivolumab. The five backbones are alternatives; your team prescribes one.

questions.q: Does nivolumab continue after surgery?
questions.a: Not automatically under this NCCP regimen. It covers at most three cycles before surgery; any later treatment needs a separate plan.

questions.q: What if a dose is delayed?
questions.a: The team reviews blood tests, symptoms and recovery. Do not assume a delay means treatment has failed or that surgery must occur on a fixed date.

chapters.title: Your treatment before surgery
chapters.intro: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

items.title: Why these medicines?
items.text: Nivolumab helps immune cells recognise cancer; chemotherapy damages dividing cells. Your prescribed backbone is gemcitabine and cisplatin.

items.title: Evidence and uncertainty
items.text: In a randomized study, adding nivolumab to chemotherapy before surgery improved survival compared with chemotherapy alone. Your team considers the exact cancer, test results, fitness and preferences.

items.title: Alternatives
items.text: Discuss surgery and other suitable treatments, clinical trials and the option of not proceeding; choices depend on the multidisciplinary assessment.

patient.title: Nivolumab, pemetrexed and carboplatin before surgery
patient.purpose: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment.

agents.name: Pemetrexed
agents.explanation: Pemetrexed blocks several enzymes that use folate to make the building blocks of DNA and RNA. This can slow or stop cancer-cell growth. Healthy cells can also be affected. Prescribed folic acid and vitamin B12 reduce important toxicities and are part of treatment.
agents.watch: Take the prescribed folic acid and attend for B12. Report mouth sores, diarrhoea, a rash, breathlessness or reduced urine; check before taking ibuprofen or other non-prescription medicines.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Skin rash; rarely serious skin reactions

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Its dose depends on target exposure (AUC) and measured or estimated kidney function; AUC is not a fixed number of milligrams. There are two planned doses in this regimen.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, nausea, hearing changes or numbness. Tell the nurse immediately about possible allergy during the infusion.

questions.q: Will I receive all five combinations?
questions.a: No. This guide is for pemetrexed and carboplatin with nivolumab. The five backbones are alternatives; your team prescribes one.

questions.q: Does nivolumab continue after surgery?
questions.a: Not automatically under this NCCP regimen. It covers at most three cycles before surgery; any later treatment needs a separate plan.

questions.q: What if a dose is delayed?
questions.a: The team reviews blood tests, symptoms and recovery. Do not assume a delay means treatment has failed or that surgery must occur on a fixed date.

items.title: Why these medicines?
items.text: Nivolumab helps immune cells recognise cancer; chemotherapy damages dividing cells. Your prescribed backbone is pemetrexed and carboplatin.

items.title: Evidence and uncertainty
items.text: In a randomized study, adding nivolumab to chemotherapy before surgery improved survival compared with chemotherapy alone. Your team considers the exact cancer, test results, fitness and preferences.

questions.q: Will I receive all five combinations?
questions.a: No. This guide is for pemetrexed and cisplatin with nivolumab. The five backbones are alternatives; your team prescribes one.

questions.q: Does nivolumab continue after surgery?
questions.a: Not automatically under this NCCP regimen. It covers at most three cycles before surgery; any later treatment needs a separate plan.

questions.q: What if a dose is delayed?
questions.a: The team reviews blood tests, symptoms and recovery. Do not assume a delay means treatment has failed or that surgery must occur on a fixed date.

chapters.title: Your treatment before surgery
chapters.intro: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

items.title: Why these medicines?
items.text: Nivolumab helps immune cells recognise cancer; chemotherapy damages dividing cells. Your prescribed backbone is pemetrexed and cisplatin.

items.title: Evidence and uncertainty
items.text: In a randomized study, adding nivolumab to chemotherapy before surgery improved survival compared with chemotherapy alone. Your team considers the exact cancer, test results, fitness and preferences.

items.title: Alternatives
items.text: Discuss surgery and other suitable treatments, clinical trials and the option of not proceeding; choices depend on the multidisciplinary assessment.

chapters.title: Treatment visits
chapters.intro: Up to three 21-day cycles. Day 1: nivolumab, pemetrexed and cisplatin. Then surgical MDT reassessment. The five listed backbones are alternatives; this guide covers only your selected combination.

items.title: Administration
items.text: Nivolumab is infused over 30 minutes before chemotherapy. Pemetrexed is infused over 10 minutes. Cisplatin is infused over one hour, with prescribed hydration before and afterwards. Blood-result review, preparation, support medicines and observation add to the visit.

items.title: Day-by-day checks

patient.title: Nivolumab, ipilimumab, pemetrexed and carboplatin
patient.purpose: This treatment aims to control metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer, help symptoms and extend life. It is usually given without an expectation of cure. The team checks the cancer subtype, molecular results, your health and your preferences before recommending this particular chemotherapy backbone.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment. Seek urgent help for new chest pain, severe muscle weakness, drooping eyelids or difficulty swallowing or breathing.

agents.name: Ipilimumab
agents.explanation: Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another control on T-cell activity. It works alongside nivolumab through a different immune checkpoint. It is given every 42 days, so it is absent from each Day 22 visit. Healthy organs can also become inflamed.
agents.watch: Report diarrhoea, tummy pain, rash, severe tiredness, headache or other new symptoms promptly. Keep your immune alert card.
risks: Immune bowel, liver, skin and hormone inflammation

agents.name: Pemetrexed
agents.explanation: Pemetrexed blocks enzymes needed to make DNA and RNA building blocks. Dividing cancer cells are affected, but healthy blood-forming and mouth-lining cells can also be injured. Prescribed folic acid and B12 reduce toxicity; do not omit them because pemetrexed is an antifolate. There are two planned doses in this regimen.
agents.watch: Low blood counts, sore mouth, rash, sickness and kidney problems can occur.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Its dose depends on target exposure (AUC) and measured or estimated kidney function; AUC is not a fixed number of milligrams. There are two planned doses in this regimen.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, nausea, hearing changes or numbness. Tell the nurse immediately about possible allergy during the infusion.

phases.label: Cycle 1 · chemotherapy on Days 1 and 22
phases.detail: The first cycle lasts 42 days: all four medicines on Day 1, then nivolumab, pemetrexed and carboplatin on Day 22. Chemotherapy ends after those two visits. From Cycle 2, nivolumab continues on Days 1 and 22 and ipilimumab on Day 1 of each 42-day cycle.

phases.label: Cycle 2 onwards · immune continuation
phases.detail: Nivolumab every 21 days; ipilimumab every 42 days. No further chemotherapy. Immune treatment continues while appropriate until the cancer progresses, side effects require stopping, or up to 24 months without progression. Plans can change after review.

day_groups.body: Nivolumab and ipilimumab are due. In Cycle 1, pemetrexed and carboplatin are also due. Checks, preparation and observation add to the infusion time.
day_groups.action: Report symptoms before treatment and confirm your support prescription.

day_groups.title: Between the first and second visits
day_groups.body: Follow the prescribed support plan after chemotherapy. Symptoms can occur at any time; do not use the date to decide they are safe.

day_groups.title: Day 22 visit · no ipilimumab
day_groups.body: In Cycle 1 this is nivolumab and the second/final chemotherapy administration. In later cycles this is nivolumab only. Blood count, kidney and liver checks remain due.
day_groups.action: Confirm the active medicines and support plan; do not repeat ipilimumab at this visit.

day_groups.title: Before the next 42-day cycle
day_groups.body: After the final pemetrexed, folate continues for 21 days. In immune-only cycles, continue to report symptoms between visits.
day_groups.action: Confirm the next Day 1 appointment and glucose/thyroid as well as usual blood checks.

support.title: Cycle 1 Days 1 and 22 · chemotherapy-containing visits
support.text: Use dedicated carboplatin AUC ≥4 NCIS row; no routine olanzapine in that row. Folic acid starts before pemetrexed, continues through both chemotherapy visits and for 21 days after the last pemetrexed dose. B12 is given in the preceding week. The source repeats B12 every three cycles if pemetrexed continues; this planned course has only two pemetrexed administrations, so do not automatically continue B12 in immune-only cycles. Your team reconciles the steroid used to prevent pemetrexed rash with the anti-sickness steroid into one clear prescription. Do not add the two schedules together or use leftover steroids yourself. Nivolumab and ipilimumab can inflame healthy organs. Report new symptoms promptly, including after treatment stops; follow-up vigilance is required for at least five months after the last dose.

support.title: Cycle 2 onwards Day 1 · nivolumab + ipilimumab every 42 days
support.text: Ipilimumab is low risk and nivolumab minimal; this combined visit is low risk. No further pemetrexed or platinum: stop/review induction antiemetics and rash steroid; complete the folate tail only. Continue immune symptom education, bloods each treatment and glucose/TFT each 42-day cycle.

support.title: Cycle 2 onwards Day 22 · nivolumab alone, between ipilimumab visits
support.text: No routine prophylactic antiemetic course for nivolumab-only minimal-risk treatment; prescribe symptom-directed rescue under local policy if needed. Ipilimumab is due at the next 42-day cycle Day 1, not every nivolumab visit. Immune toxicity can still occur between ipilimumab visits; the joint hold rule remains relevant.

questions.q: Will chemotherapy continue for months?
questions.a: The planned pemetrexed/platinum course is two administrations, on Days 1 and 22 of Cycle 1. Immune treatment can continue afterwards with a different support plan.

questions.q: Why is ipilimumab absent from some visits?
questions.a: Nivolumab is every 21 days; ipilimumab every 42 days. Day 22 has no ipilimumab. A withheld immune dose is a separate safety decision requiring team review.

questions.q: How will we know whether it is helping?
questions.a: Ask about the goals, scan plan and what would lead to continuing, changing or stopping. Side effects do not reliably show treatment response.

questions.q: Can I decide from this guide whether treatment is safe today?
questions.a: No. Your team must interpret symptoms, bloods, previous reactions and the current prescribing protocol. Omitted results are not presumed normal.

questions.q: What if I miss folic acid or a steroid dose?
questions.a: Contact your treatment team or pharmacy for an individual plan. Do not double doses or combine separate steroid schedules yourself.

questions.q: Which risks continue after treatment?
questions.a: Nivolumab and ipilimumab can inflame healthy organs. Report new symptoms promptly, including after treatment stops; follow-up vigilance is required for at least five months after the last dose. Ask about follow-up for any lasting nerve, hearing, kidney, hormone or other problems.

items.title: What do the cancer terms mean?
items.text: Metastatic means cancer has spread beyond where it started. NSCLC is a broad lung-cancer group; non-squamous describes one histology, often adenocarcinoma. First-line means the first systemic treatment for this setting. The pathology and molecular results help determine whether this exact pemetrexed combination suits your cancer.

items.title: What does the evidence mean for me?
items.text: In CheckMate 9LA, the strategy of two immune medicines with a short chemotherapy course helped people live longer than chemotherapy alone. The study included different histologies and platinum medicines. It cannot tell exactly what benefit you will have, or prove that this particular platinum is better for you.

items.title: What are the alternatives?
items.text: Ask how tumour tests, fitness and your priorities affect the options, including other drug combinations, targeted treatment when relevant, a clinical trial or symptom-focused care. Support for breathlessness, pain, appetite and emotional concerns can accompany anticancer treatment.

chapters.title: Before the first visit
chapters.intro: The preventive medicines and baseline review are part of the treatment.

items.title: Describe your usual health
items.text: Tell the team about your usual breathing and bowel pattern, autoimmune illness, lung inflammation, infections, nerve or hearing symptoms, diabetes, and all prescription or non-prescription medicines. This helps identify a new problem promptly.

items.title: Folate, B12 and steroid plan
items.text: Folic acid starts before pemetrexed, continues through both chemotherapy visits and for 21 days after the last pemetrexed dose. B12 is given in the preceding week. The source repeats B12 every three cycles if pemetrexed continues; this planned course has only two pemetrexed administrations, so do not automatically continue B12 in immune-only cycles. Your team reconciles the steroid used to prevent pemetrexed rash with the anti-sickness steroid into one clear prescription. Do not add the two schedules together or use leftover steroids yourself.

items.title: Prepare contact and practical support
items.text: Keep your oncology and out-of-hours instructions, a thermometer, treatment names and immune alert card available. Arrange blood tests, transport and help at home where needed. Ask what to do if a support medicine is missed; do not double a dose without advice.

chapters.title: Two chemotherapy visits, then continuing immunotherapy
chapters.intro: The first cycle lasts 42 days: all four medicines on Day 1, then nivolumab, pemetrexed and carboplatin on Day 22. Chemotherapy ends after those two visits. From Cycle 2, nivolumab continues on Days 1 and 22 and ipilimumab on Day 1 of each 42-day cycle.

items.title: Day 1 and Day 22 differ
items.text: Cycle 1 Day 1 includes all four medicines. Day 22 is three weeks later and includes nivolumab plus the second and final planned chemotherapy doses, but no ipilimumab. A 42-day cycle is six weeks.

items.title: The next 42-day cycles
items.text: From Cycle 2, Day 1 includes nivolumab and ipilimumab. Day 22 includes nivolumab only. No pemetrexed or platinum is planned in this continuation phase. The support medicines change too; check the updated prescription.

items.title: How long does treatment last?
items.text: Immune treatment continues while appropriate until the cancer progresses, side effects require stopping, or up to 24 months without progression. Plans can change after review. The team reviews benefit, symptoms and scans. A delay can allow investigation or recovery. It does not mean you have failed treatment.

chapters.title: What the checks are looking for
chapters.intro: Different checks assess safety today, possible toxicity and cancer response.

items.title: Blood count, kidney and liver
items.text: Blood counts and kidney/liver tests are checked before each Day 1 and Day 22 treatment. Blood counts show infection-fighting cells, oxygen-carrying cells and platelets. Kidney results influence chemotherapy safety. Normal results from a previous visit do not rule out a new problem.

items.title: Hormones and immune effects
items.text: Glucose and thyroid tests are checked before each 42-day cycle. The baseline assessment includes morning cortisol and hepatitis tests. New symptoms can require extra tests between planned visits; routine blood tests alone cannot exclude all immune side effects.

items.title: Scans and decisions
items.text: Your consultant sets the scan schedule. The team considers symptoms, examination, results and what matters to you. Side effects are not a reliable measure of how well treatment is controlling cancer.

chapters.title: Effects around the chemotherapy visits
chapters.intro: These are selected possibilities, not a forecast or a complete medicine leaflet.

items.title: Sickness, appetite and constipation
items.text: Take preventive anti-sickness medicines as prescribed. Tell the team if they do not control symptoms. Persistent vomiting, difficulty keeping fluids down or much less urine need prompt advice. Some anti-sickness and pain medicines cause constipation; ask for a bowel plan.

items.title: Blood counts and infection
items.text: Fever, shivers or suddenly feeling unwell need immediate oncology advice, even with a normal temperature. Counts can fall between visits and cannot be judged from the calendar. Report unexpected bruising, bleeding or worsening breathlessness.

items.title: Mouth, skin and tiredness
items.text: Use gentle mouth care and report ulcers, painful swallowing, rash or reduced intake. Balance rest with manageable activity. Marked or sudden weakness needs assessment: fatigue can also be caused by infection, anaemia or immune hormone problems.

items.title: Kidneys, hearing and nerves
items.text: Carboplatin dosing depends on kidney function. Tell the team about reduced urine, new ringing in the ears, hearing loss, tingling or numbness before another chemotherapy dose.

chapters.title: Immune effects need early reporting
chapters.intro: Nivolumab and ipilimumab can inflame healthy organs. Report new symptoms promptly, including after treatment stops; follow-up vigilance is required for at least five months after the last dose.

items.title: Breathing, bowel, skin and urine
items.text: New cough or breathlessness, diarrhoea, blood or mucus in stool, severe abdominal pain, yellow eyes, dark urine, reduced urine or swelling need prompt assessment. Do not assume these are ordinary chemotherapy effects. Blistering or peeling skin or sores in the eyes or mouth need urgent care.

items.title: Hormones, heart, muscles and nerves
items.text: Report unusual weakness, persistent headache, dizziness, marked thirst, frequent urination, palpitations, muscle weakness or vision changes. Severe chest pain, collapse, confusion or major breathing difficulty needs emergency care. Some hormone effects require long-term replacement.

items.title: Treatment may need to pause
items.text: The team may withhold both immune medicines, investigate and prescribe steroids or other treatment. This is different from the short preventive steroid course around chemotherapy. Do not start leftover steroids, change their dose or abruptly stop a prescribed course.

chapters.title: Living with treatment
chapters.intro: The aim is to fit care around the things that matter to you.

items.title: Food, fluids, work and movement
items.text: Ask for help with weight loss, reduced appetite, work adjustments, transport or household tasks. A fixed fluid target is not suitable for everyone. Do not drive if dizzy, very tired or affected by sedating medicines; cisplatin anti-sickness treatment can include olanzapine.

items.title: Fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding
items.text: Discuss fertility before treatment where relevant. Ask for a written contraception plan covering all four medicines and the period after treatment. Report possible pregnancy promptly and do not breastfeed unless your team confirms it is safe.

items.title: Support and choices
items.text: Ask for an interpreter, accessible information, psychological support or a trusted person to join appointments. Discuss alternatives, expected benefits and lasting harms. You can revisit your preferences as treatment continues.

chapters.title: Care after a drug stops
chapters.intro: Stopping chemotherapy or immunotherapy changes the plan but does not immediately remove all risks.

items.title: After the second pemetrexed dose
items.text: Finish the prescribed 21-day folic-acid tail after the last pemetrexed. Review anti-sickness and rash-steroid stop dates. B12 is not automatically continued just because immune therapy continues.

items.title: After the last immune dose
items.text: Nivolumab and ipilimumab can inflame healthy organs. Report new symptoms promptly, including after treatment stops; follow-up vigilance is required for at least five months after the last dose. Keep the alert card and tell other healthcare professionals about both immune medicines. Ask who will arrange follow-up and review any unresolved symptoms.

items.title: Use your team’s urgent instructions
items.text: When you call, state your treatment names, last treatment date, what changed, temperature if known, and whether you can drink and pass urine. Do not delay calling while gathering every detail.

evidence.title: Why this treatment is offered
evidence.intro: The combined strategy improved survival compared with chemotherapy in the trial population, with some durable responses. Benefits and harms vary between people.
evidence.interpretation: The study tested the combined strategy across different lung-cancer histologies and chemotherapy choices. Your own expected benefit depends on your cancer and health.
evidence.population: Previously untreated metastatic/recurrent NSCLC without sensitising EGFR/ALK alterations.
evidence.limitations: This is not a personal survival forecast or a direct comparison of carboplatin with cisplatin.

rationale.summary: Nivolumab blocks PD-1 and ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, supporting T-cell antitumour activity through different checkpoint pathways. Pemetrexed inhibits nucleotide synthesis and carboplatin damages DNA. The trial combines limited initial chemotherapy with continuing dual immunotherapy; this rationale does not predict individual response.

evidence.population: 719 previously untreated adults with stage IV/recurrent NSCLC without sensitising EGFR/ALK alterations; mixed squamous and non-squamous histologies.
evidence.comparison: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab and two cycles of histology-based platinum-doublet chemotherapy (361) versus four chemotherapy cycles (358); optional pemetrexed maintenance in the control non-squamous population.
evidence.applicability: Supports the overall first-line strategy. The pemetrexed protocols correspond to the non-squamous chemotherapy backbone studied; overall results pool histologies and platinum choices. No separate randomized benefit estimate for this exact carboplatin backbone is asserted.

endpoints.metric: Overall randomized population, final six-year analysis
endpoints.result_text: HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.63–0.87); six-year survival 16% versus 10%, minimum follow-up 68.6 months.
endpoints.interpretation: Population-level randomized comparison of the complete treatment strategies, not a personal survival prediction or a cisplatin-versus-carboplatin comparison.
endpoints.analysis_status: Final six-year follow-up; published 29 May 2025.

endpoints.interpretation: Descriptive subgroup result; does not isolate pemetrexed/carboplatin from pemetrexed/cisplatin or establish comparative benefit between platinum choices.
endpoints.analysis_status: Final follow-up subgroup analysis; retain subgroup limitations.

evidence.qualitative_result: The combined strategy improved survival compared with chemotherapy in the trial population, with some durable responses. Benefits and harms vary between people.
limitations: The whole-trial result includes squamous and non-squamous disease and different chemotherapy backbones.
Non-squamous subgroup data do not establish a separate survival effect for carboplatin versus cisplatin.
Trial participants and treatment selection differ from an individual patient; the reported survival proportions are not individual benefit predictions.
The current NCCP broad NSCLC wording must not be treated as evidence for a histologically inappropriate pemetrexed backbone.
evidence.harms: Combining chemotherapy with dual checkpoint blockade introduces cytotoxic and immune-mediated harms; important inflammation can affect multiple organs and require hospital care or permanent treatment cessation. Final follow-up reported no new safety signals; this does not imply no risk.

patient.title: Nivolumab, ipilimumab, pemetrexed and cisplatin
patient.purpose: This treatment aims to control metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer, help symptoms and extend life. It is usually given without an expectation of cure. The team checks the cancer subtype, molecular results, your health and your preferences before recommending this particular chemotherapy backbone.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment. Seek urgent help for new chest pain, severe muscle weakness, drooping eyelids or difficulty swallowing or breathing.

agents.name: Ipilimumab
agents.explanation: Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another control on T-cell activity. It works alongside nivolumab through a different immune checkpoint. It is given every 42 days, so it is absent from each Day 22 visit. Healthy organs can also become inflamed.
agents.watch: Report diarrhoea, tummy pain, rash, severe tiredness, headache or other new symptoms promptly. Keep your immune alert card.
risks: Immune bowel, liver, skin and hormone inflammation

agents.name: Pemetrexed
agents.explanation: Pemetrexed blocks enzymes needed to make DNA and RNA building blocks. Dividing cancer cells are affected, but healthy blood-forming and mouth-lining cells can also be injured. Prescribed folic acid and B12 reduce toxicity; do not omit them because pemetrexed is an antifolate. There are two planned doses in this regimen.
agents.watch: Low blood counts, sore mouth, rash, sickness and kidney problems can occur.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Kidney injury, changes in salts in the blood, hearing damage and nerve symptoms are important risks. Extra fluids and electrolyte checks are part of treatment. There are two planned doses in this regimen.
agents.watch: Report reduced urine, vomiting, ringing in the ears, hearing change or numbness. Hydration instructions are individual.

phases.label: Cycle 1 · chemotherapy on Days 1 and 22
phases.detail: The first cycle lasts 42 days: all four medicines on Day 1, then nivolumab, pemetrexed and cisplatin on Day 22. Chemotherapy ends after those two visits. From Cycle 2, nivolumab continues on Days 1 and 22 and ipilimumab on Day 1 of each 42-day cycle.

phases.label: Cycle 2 onwards · immune continuation
phases.detail: Nivolumab every 21 days; ipilimumab every 42 days. No further chemotherapy. Immune treatment continues while appropriate until the cancer progresses, side effects require stopping, or up to 24 months without progression. Plans can change after review.

questions.q: Will chemotherapy continue for months?
questions.a: The planned pemetrexed/platinum course is two administrations, on Days 1 and 22 of Cycle 1. Immune treatment can continue afterwards with a different support plan.

questions.q: Why is ipilimumab absent from some visits?
questions.a: Nivolumab is every 21 days; ipilimumab every 42 days. Day 22 has no ipilimumab. A withheld immune dose is a separate safety decision requiring team review.

questions.q: How will we know whether it is helping?
questions.a: Ask about the goals, scan plan and what would lead to continuing, changing or stopping. Side effects do not reliably show treatment response.

questions.q: Can I decide from this guide whether treatment is safe today?
questions.a: No. Your team must interpret symptoms, bloods, previous reactions and the current prescribing protocol. Omitted results are not presumed normal.

questions.q: What if I miss folic acid or a steroid dose?
questions.a: Contact your treatment team or pharmacy for an individual plan. Do not double doses or combine separate steroid schedules yourself.

questions.q: Which risks continue after treatment?
questions.a: Nivolumab and ipilimumab can inflame healthy organs. Report new symptoms promptly, including after treatment stops; follow-up vigilance is required for at least five months after the last dose. Ask about follow-up for any lasting nerve, hearing, kidney, hormone or other problems.

chapters.title: Why this combination is offered
chapters.intro: This treatment aims to control metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer, help symptoms and extend life. It is usually given without an expectation of cure. The team checks the cancer subtype, molecular results, your health and your preferences before recommending this particular chemotherapy backbone.

items.title: What do the cancer terms mean?
items.text: Metastatic means cancer has spread beyond where it started. NSCLC is a broad lung-cancer group; non-squamous describes one histology, often adenocarcinoma. First-line means the first systemic treatment for this setting. The pathology and molecular results help determine whether this exact pemetrexed combination suits your cancer.

items.title: What does the evidence mean for me?
items.text: In CheckMate 9LA, the strategy of two immune medicines with a short chemotherapy course helped people live longer than chemotherapy alone. The study included different histologies and platinum medicines. It cannot tell exactly what benefit you will have, or prove that this particular platinum is better for you.

items.title: What are the alternatives?
items.text: Ask how tumour tests, fitness and your priorities affect the options, including other drug combinations, targeted treatment when relevant, a clinical trial or symptom-focused care. Support for breathlessness, pain, appetite and emotional concerns can accompany anticancer treatment.

chapters.title: Before the first visit
chapters.intro: The preventive medicines and baseline review are part of the treatment.

items.title: Describe your usual health
items.text: Tell the team about your usual breathing and bowel pattern, autoimmune illness, lung inflammation, infections, nerve or hearing symptoms, diabetes, and all prescription or non-prescription medicines. This helps identify a new problem promptly.

items.title: Folate, B12 and steroid plan
items.text: Folic acid starts before pemetrexed, continues through both chemotherapy visits and for 21 days after the last pemetrexed dose. B12 is given in the preceding week. The source repeats B12 every three cycles if pemetrexed continues; this planned course has only two pemetrexed administrations, so do not automatically continue B12 in immune-only cycles. Your team reconciles the steroid used to prevent pemetrexed rash with the anti-sickness steroid into one clear prescription. Do not add the two schedules together or use leftover steroids yourself.

items.title: Prepare contact and practical support
items.text: Keep your oncology and out-of-hours instructions, a thermometer, treatment names and immune alert card available. Arrange blood tests, transport and help at home where needed. Ask what to do if a support medicine is missed; do not double a dose without advice.

chapters.title: Two chemotherapy visits, then continuing immunotherapy
chapters.intro: The first cycle lasts 42 days: all four medicines on Day 1, then nivolumab, pemetrexed and cisplatin on Day 22. Chemotherapy ends after those two visits. From Cycle 2, nivolumab continues on Days 1 and 22 and ipilimumab on Day 1 of each 42-day cycle.

items.title: Day 1 and Day 22 differ
items.text: Cycle 1 Day 1 includes all four medicines. Day 22 is three weeks later and includes nivolumab plus the second and final planned chemotherapy doses, but no ipilimumab. A 42-day cycle is six weeks.

items.title: The next 42-day cycles
items.text: From Cycle 2, Day 1 includes nivolumab and ipilimumab. Day 22 includes nivolumab only. No pemetrexed or platinum is planned in this continuation phase. The support medicines change too; check the updated prescription.

items.title: How long does treatment last?
items.text: Immune treatment continues while appropriate until the cancer progresses, side effects require stopping, or up to 24 months without progression. Plans can change after review. The team reviews benefit, symptoms and scans. A delay can allow investigation or recovery. It does not mean you have failed treatment.

chapters.title: What the checks are looking for
chapters.intro: Different checks assess safety today, possible toxicity and cancer response.

items.title: Blood count, kidney and liver
items.text: Blood counts and kidney/liver tests are checked before each Day 1 and Day 22 treatment. Blood counts show infection-fighting cells, oxygen-carrying cells and platelets. Kidney results influence chemotherapy safety. Normal results from a previous visit do not rule out a new problem.

items.title: Hormones and immune effects
items.text: Glucose and thyroid tests are checked before each 42-day cycle. The baseline assessment includes morning cortisol and hepatitis tests. New symptoms can require extra tests between planned visits; routine blood tests alone cannot exclude all immune side effects.

items.title: Scans and decisions
items.text: Your consultant sets the scan schedule. The team considers symptoms, examination, results and what matters to you. Side effects are not a reliable measure of how well treatment is controlling cancer.

chapters.title: Effects around the chemotherapy visits
chapters.intro: These are selected possibilities, not a forecast or a complete medicine leaflet.

items.title: Sickness, appetite and constipation
items.text: Take preventive anti-sickness medicines as prescribed. Tell the team if they do not control symptoms. Persistent vomiting, difficulty keeping fluids down or much less urine need prompt advice. Some anti-sickness and pain medicines cause constipation; ask for a bowel plan.

items.title: Blood counts and infection
items.text: Fever, shivers or suddenly feeling unwell need immediate oncology advice, even with a normal temperature. Counts can fall between visits and cannot be judged from the calendar. Report unexpected bruising, bleeding or worsening breathlessness.

items.title: Mouth, skin and tiredness
items.text: Use gentle mouth care and report ulcers, painful swallowing, rash or reduced intake. Balance rest with manageable activity. Marked or sudden weakness needs assessment: fatigue can also be caused by infection, anaemia or immune hormone problems.

items.title: Kidneys, hearing and nerves
items.text: Cisplatin can injure kidneys and affect blood salts, hearing and nerves. Fluids before and after the infusion reduce particular risks, and your fluid advice is individual. Tell the team about reduced urine, new ringing in the ears, hearing loss, tingling or numbness before another chemotherapy dose.

chapters.title: Immune effects need early reporting
chapters.intro: Nivolumab and ipilimumab can inflame healthy organs. Report new symptoms promptly, including after treatment stops; follow-up vigilance is required for at least five months after the last dose.

items.title: Breathing, bowel, skin and urine
items.text: New cough or breathlessness, diarrhoea, blood or mucus in stool, severe abdominal pain, yellow eyes, dark urine, reduced urine or swelling need prompt assessment. Do not assume these are ordinary chemotherapy effects. Blistering or peeling skin or sores in the eyes or mouth need urgent care.

items.title: Hormones, heart, muscles and nerves
items.text: Report unusual weakness, persistent headache, dizziness, marked thirst, frequent urination, palpitations, muscle weakness or vision changes. Severe chest pain, collapse, confusion or major breathing difficulty needs emergency care. Some hormone effects require long-term replacement.

items.title: Treatment may need to pause
items.text: The team may withhold both immune medicines, investigate and prescribe steroids or other treatment. This is different from the short preventive steroid course around chemotherapy. Do not start leftover steroids, change their dose or abruptly stop a prescribed course.

chapters.title: Living with treatment
chapters.intro: The aim is to fit care around the things that matter to you.

items.title: Food, fluids, work and movement
items.text: Ask for help with weight loss, reduced appetite, work adjustments, transport or household tasks. A fixed fluid target is not suitable for everyone. Do not drive if dizzy, very tired or affected by sedating medicines; cisplatin anti-sickness treatment can include olanzapine.

items.title: Fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding
items.text: Discuss fertility before treatment where relevant. Ask for a written contraception plan covering all four medicines and the period after treatment. Report possible pregnancy promptly and do not breastfeed unless your team confirms it is safe.

items.title: Support and choices
items.text: Ask for an interpreter, accessible information, psychological support or a trusted person to join appointments. Discuss alternatives, expected benefits and lasting harms. You can revisit your preferences as treatment continues.

chapters.title: Care after a drug stops
chapters.intro: Stopping chemotherapy or immunotherapy changes the plan but does not immediately remove all risks.

items.title: After the second pemetrexed dose
items.text: Finish the prescribed 21-day folic-acid tail after the last pemetrexed. Review anti-sickness and rash-steroid stop dates. B12 is not automatically continued just because immune therapy continues.

items.title: After the last immune dose
items.text: Nivolumab and ipilimumab can inflame healthy organs. Report new symptoms promptly, including after treatment stops; follow-up vigilance is required for at least five months after the last dose. Keep the alert card and tell other healthcare professionals about both immune medicines. Ask who will arrange follow-up and review any unresolved symptoms.

items.title: Use your team’s urgent instructions
items.text: When you call, state your treatment names, last treatment date, what changed, temperature if known, and whether you can drink and pass urine. Do not delay calling while gathering every detail.

evidence.title: Why this treatment is offered
evidence.intro: The combined strategy improved survival compared with chemotherapy in the trial population, with some durable responses. Benefits and harms vary between people.
evidence.interpretation: The study tested the combined strategy across different lung-cancer histologies and chemotherapy choices. Your own expected benefit depends on your cancer and health.
evidence.population: Previously untreated metastatic/recurrent NSCLC without sensitising EGFR/ALK alterations.
evidence.limitations: This is not a personal survival forecast or a direct comparison of carboplatin with cisplatin.

patient.indication_text: First-line metastatic NSCLC in adults without a sensitising EGFR mutation or ALK translocation. Current NCCP wording is histology-broad; the suitability of this pemetrexed backbone still requires explicit histology review.
